scope: Reference alignment and targeted factual repair of author-authorized adoption. Access levels are per note; this is not full-text verification of every cited work or certification of private memoir.

notes.definition: Carl Sagan, *Cosmos* (1980), as quoted in Kate Howells, [“We’re made of starstuff. What does that mean?”](https://www.planetary.org/articles/were-made-of-starstuff-what-does-that-mean), The Planetary Society, 9 November 2025. Capitalization follows this chapter.
notes.evidence: 2026-10-23: institutional reproduction of the quotation inspected; wording matches apart from capitalization. Original episode/book locator not independently established; note explicitly identifies the reproduction.

notes.definition: W. H. Zurek, [“Decoherence, einselection, and the quantum origins of the classical”](https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/0105127), *Reviews of Modern Physics* 75 (2003): 715–775, on environmental correlations and stable records. “Registration” here does not imply consciousness or a record that must last indefinitely.
notes.evidence: Prior verification: Chapter 1 catalog zurek2003decoherence and Φ records, abstract and record/pointer-state discussion. Reused 2026-10-23, not newly read cover to cover.

notes.definition: Particle Data Group, [“Inflation”](https://pdg.lbl.gov/2025/reviews/rpp2025-rev-inflation.pdf), §§23.1–23.2 (2025), and [“Higgs Boson”](https://pdg.lbl.gov/2025/reviews/rpp2025-rev-higgs-boson.pdf), §§11.1–11.2; Planck Collaboration, [“Planck 2018 results. VI. Cosmological parameters”](https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.06209), *Astronomy & Astrophysics* 641 (2020): A6. Inflation and proposed earlier force-unification stages do not have the evidentiary status of the hot thermal history.
notes.evidence: Prior PDG passage checks (2026-10-04); Planck abstract and cosmological parameters freshly checked 2026-10-23. Approximate recombination time is the standard model timeline, not a measurement of an absolute beginning.

notes.definition: For the chronology and Grossmann’s mathematical role, see Tilman Sauer, [“‘Before Everything was Completely Clear, We Had a Few Arguments.’—Emmy Noether, David Hilbert and Felix Klein”](https://doi.org/10.1007/s44007-025-00166-w), *La Matematica* 4 (2025): 674–701, §2; and Galina Weinstein, [“Max Born, Albert Einstein and Hermann Minkowski’s Space-Time Formalism of Special Relativity”](https://arxiv.org/abs/1210.6929) (2012). Einstein’s special relativity dates to 1905, Minkowski’s spacetime presentation to 1908, and the Einstein–Grossmann collaboration to 1912–1913.
notes.evidence: 2026-10-23: Sauer archival study introduction/section 2 inspected; Weinstein arXiv abstract, author and complete title freshly verified. No claim that Minkowski preceded Einstein’s 1905 theory.

notes.definition: [“Modal Logic,”](https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/logic-modal/) *Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy*, §§2 and 7, on modal systems and reflexive accessibility. The implication $p\to\Diamond p$ holds in suitable systems, including those with axiom T; it is not a theorem of every modal logic. It does not establish that all consistent possibilities are instantiated.
notes.evidence: 2026-10-23: expert-authored reference entry §§2/7 inspected. The traditional Latin maxim is used as a maxim, without attributing it to an unverified medieval author.

notes.definition: David J. C. MacKay, [*Information Theory, Inference, and Learning Algorithms*](https://sites.stat.columbia.edu/gelman/bayescomputation/mackay.pdf) (Cambridge University Press, 2003), ch. 28, especially pp. 344–348 and eq. 28.7. The Bayesian evidence averages predictions over parameter priors; an Occam factor can arise even with equal prior probabilities for the competing models. A cosmological simplicity weighting is a further hypothesis.
notes.evidence: 2026-10-23: downloaded published textbook, third printing of first edition; pp. 343–348 read directly using PDF text extraction, especially model-prior distinction on p.344 and evidence integral p.348.

notes.definition: Sean M. Carroll, [“Why Boltzmann Brains Are Bad”](https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.00850) (2017). The problem depends on cosmological dynamics, fluctuations and how observers are counted; it is not a consequence of “chance” alone.
notes.evidence: Prior abstract check recorded in possibility SOURCE_LEDGER.md, poss-bb. Used for problem scope, not as proof of a solution.

notes.definition: Jürgen Schmidhuber, [“Algorithmic Theories of Everything”](https://people.idsia.ch/~juergen/toesv2/), version 2 (2000), especially §6; Markus P. Müller, [“Law without law: from observer states to physics via algorithmic information theory”](https://arxiv.org/html/1712.01826v5), *Quantum* 4 (2020): 301, especially §§2–4 and 8. These offer explicit, differing algorithmic frameworks, not an established measure on all logically possible worlds. Description length, thermodynamic multiplicity and observer typicality are separate choices.
notes.evidence: Prior primary text checks: catalog schmidhuber2000algorithmic and possibility ledger poss-muller. Selected full sections read in earlier research; no universal minimal-complexity/anthropic conclusion credited to either.

notes.definition: David Lewis, [“Anselm and Actuality”](https://www.andrewmbailey.com/dkl/Anselm_and_Actuality.pdf), *Noûs* 4 (1970): 175–188, especially pp. 184–185. The indexical account of “actual” is Lewis’s philosophical position, not a physical result or a derivation of the author’s conjecture.
notes.evidence: 2026-10-23: original-text indexed excerpt pp.184–185 inspected, including comparison with here, I and present.

notes.definition: Gunnar Jeschke, [*Statistical Thermodynamics*, §7.2, “Entropic Elasticity”](https://chem.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Physical_and_Theoretical_Chemistry_Textbook_Maps/Statistical_Thermodynamics_%28Jeschke%29/07%3A_Macromolecules/7.02%3A_Entropic_Elasticity). For an ideal chain whose internal energy is independent of extension, $F=U-TS$. This chapter’s $f=\partial F/\partial L=-T(\partial S/\partial L)_T$ is the outward holding force; the inward restoring force has the opposite sign. Real rubber also has energetic contributions.
notes.evidence: 2026-10-23: author teaching text, entropy/free-energy derivation and ideal-chain assumption inspected. Source writes inward restoring force; chapter explicitly adopts outward holding convention.

notes.definition: David Tong, [*Statistical Physics*, ch. 1](https://www.damtp.cam.ac.uk/user/tong/statphys/one.pdf), §§1.2.1, 1.2.5 and 1.3: entropy, the Vienna tombstone and the canonical ensemble. The ratio shown is for individual microstates in a canonical distribution at temperature $T$; probabilities of grouped energy levels also include their degeneracies.
notes.evidence: 2026-10-23: author lecture PDF, cited sections and canonical formula inspected. Units and ensemble assumptions corrected in body.

notes.definition: Alain Connes and Carlo Rovelli, [“Von Neumann algebra automorphisms and time-thermodynamics relation in general covariant quantum theories”](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/9406019), *Classical and Quantum Gravity* 11 (1994): 2899–2917. In the density-matrix setting, $K=-\ln\rho$ is defined on the support of $\rho$; for a Gibbs state, $K=H/(k_B T)+\ln Z$. Modular flow motivates their thermal-time hypothesis; it is not a demonstrated origin of physical time.
notes.evidence: Prior selected full-text check, possibility ledger thermal-time entry; 2026-10-23 abstract/introduction rechecked. Formula is the finite/density-matrix specialization, not a claim all operator algebras possess density matrices.

notes.definition: Ted Jacobson, [“Thermodynamics of Spacetime: The Einstein Equation of State”](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/9504004), *Physical Review Letters* 75 (1995): 1260–1263; Erik Verlinde, [“On the Origin of Gravity and the Laws of Newton”](https://arxiv.org/abs/1001.0785), *Journal of High Energy Physics* (2011), article 029. Their assumptions and proposals differ; neither establishes that every interaction arises from bare possibility.
notes.evidence: Jacobson: prior abstract/derivation-scope check in possibility ledger. Verlinde: abstract and publication metadata inspected 2026-10-23. Described as proposals, not observationally established replacements.

notes.definition: Brookhaven National Laboratory, [*The Bulletin Board*, 25 February 1964](https://www.bnl.gov/bnlweb/pubaf/bulletin/files/1964/19640225.pdf), pp. 1–2, describes the 80-inch hydrogen bubble chamber, particle tracks and scanning of photographs. The Yale employment, age, plaque and family recollections are the author’s; the particular experiment his mother worked on has not been identified.
notes.evidence: Contemporary BNL primary account checked in prior catalog and searched freshly 2026-10-23. Public apparatus source does not verify private memoir or a specific scanning assignment.

notes.definition: V. E. Barnes et al., [“Observation of a Hyperon with Strangeness Minus Three”](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.12.204), *Physical Review Letters* 12 (1964): 204–206; Brookhaven’s [contemporary account](https://www.bnl.gov/bnlweb/pubaf/bulletin/files/1964/19640225.pdf), pp. 1–2. The Ω⁻ completed the baryon decuplet anticipated through the symmetry work of Gell-Mann and, independently, Ne’eman. Its possible appearance in the mother’s later films remains explicitly conjectural.
notes.evidence: BNL primary report/prediction/apparatus verified in catalog bnl1964omega; PDG quark model corroborates decuplet. Barnes original metadata verified; not represented as independently read in full this run.

notes.definition: Murray Gell-Mann, “A Schematic Model of Baryons and Mesons” (1964), and George Zweig’s independent 1964 CERN proposals; see David Gross’s [2004 Nobel lecture](https://www.nobelprize.org/uploads/2024/10/gross-lecture-1.pdf), historical discussion of the Eightfold Way and quarks, and the PDG [“Quark Model”](https://pdg.lbl.gov/2025/reviews/rpp2025-rev-quark-model.pdf). Gell-Mann borrowed “quark” from James Joyce’s *Finnegans Wake*.
notes.evidence: Prior catalog gross2004qcd indexed author lecture passage and PDG quark sections checked. Original papers not newly read; note uses the author lecture and PDG as supporting access sources.

notes.definition: Particle Data Group, [“Quark Model”](https://pdg.lbl.gov/2025/reviews/rpp2025-rev-quark-model.pdf) (2025), discussion of color and baryon wavefunctions. The color part supplies the antisymmetry needed by the total state of the ground-state Ω⁻. Different color states do not turn identical strange quarks into different particle species.
notes.evidence: Prior primary review check, pdg2025quark; fresh Nobel 2004 technical-background excerpts support color/Pauli. Main text corrected accordingly.

notes.definition: SLAC, [“Milestones”](https://ahro.slac.stanford.edu/resources/slac-history/milestones), 1968 entry; Jerome I. Friedman, [1990 Nobel lecture](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/1990/friedman/lecture/), on the SLAC–MIT deep-inelastic scattering experiments. Pointlike constituents were inferred through scattering, not directly photographed.
notes.evidence: 2026-10-23: official SLAC chronology excerpt inspected; Nobel lecture is the original investigator’s further-reading source, not fully read this run.

notes.definition: DESY, [“40 years of gluon”](https://www.desy.de/news/backgrounders/40_years_of_gluon/DESYinform05-11-engl_Web_eng.html/?printversion=1), and Paul Söding, [“On the discovery of the gluon”](https://bib-pubdb1.desy.de/record/92607/files/EPJH35.pdf) (2010). Three-jet evidence emerged at PETRA in 1979 through TASSO, JADE, MARK-J and PLUTO.
notes.evidence: 2026-10-23: official DESY history and indexed discoverer-historian paper passages inspected; chronology and collaborative credit checked.

notes.definition: Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences, [scientific background to the 2004 Nobel Prize in Physics](https://www.nobelprize.org/uploads/2018/06/advanced-physicsprize2004.pdf), on asymptotic freedom and QCD. At large separations, the approximately linear confining potential means increasing stored energy, not an indefinitely increasing force. This is not the entropy-driven rubber-band mechanism discussed earlier.
notes.evidence: 2026-10-23: technical-background excerpts inspected; prior Gross/QCD catalog supports scope. Corrected force/potential distinction.

notes.definition: Chris Quigg, [“Origins of Mass”](https://arxiv.org/abs/0704.2232) (2007); S. Dürr et al., [“Ab Initio Determination of Light Hadron Masses”](https://arxiv.org/abs/0906.3599), *Science* 322 (2008): 1224–1227. Most proton mass comes from QCD dynamics, rather than the small masses of its quarks; “binding energy” alone can misleadingly suggest a simple negative mass defect.
notes.evidence: Prior author review and lattice-paper abstract checks in chapter physics review/catalog. Quigg original publication metadata retained; no cover-to-cover claim.

notes.definition: David Tong, [*Quantum Field Theory*](https://www.damtp.cam.ac.uk/user/tong/qft.htm), §§2 and 4, on quantized free fields and the Dirac field. Electrons share intrinsic particle properties; they need not occupy the same state or have the same momentum.
notes.evidence: Prior selected lecture-text checks, tong2006qft. Unqualified identical-state inference repaired.

notes.definition: Emmy Noether, [“Invariante Variationsprobleme”](https://arxiv.org/abs/physics/0503066) (1918), Theorems I and II, English translation by M. A. Tavel (1971); Tong, [*Quantum Field Theory*](https://www.damtp.cam.ac.uk/user/tong/qft.htm), §1.3.1. The theorem concerns continuous symmetries of the action. Local conservation in general relativity does not guarantee a globally conserved total energy for an expanding universe.
notes.evidence: Original theorem/translation identity and Tong passage previously checked. 1918 chronology freshly corroborated through Rowe/Sauer archival research, replacing source’s unsupported 1915 proof date.

notes.definition: American Physical Society, [*APS News*, March 2013](https://print.aps.org/pdf/2013-03.pdf), “This Month in Physics History,” on Noether’s Göttingen years, reports Hilbert’s bathhouse remark. See also Tilman Sauer’s [2025 archival study](https://doi.org/10.1007/s44007-025-00166-w). “Reportedly” distinguishes the familiar recollection from a contemporaneous verbatim transcript.
notes.evidence: 2026-10-23: APS indexed quotation and employment narrative inspected; Sauer archival discussion read. Exact wording remains a reported historical anecdote, not transcript-certified.

notes.definition: Eugene Wigner, [“On Unitary Representations of the Inhomogeneous Lorentz Group”](https://www.math.utoronto.ca/mgualt/courses/25-QM/docs/Wigner-1939.pdf), *Annals of Mathematics* 40 (1939): 149–204. For the massive-particle case used here, irreducible Poincaré representations are classified by mass and spin; momenta and spin components can transform between observers.
notes.evidence: Prior original-paper scope/metadata check in wigner1939representations. General-reader summary narrowed to invariant labels, not identical appearances.

notes.definition: J. H. Christenson, J. W. Cronin, V. L. Fitch and R. Turlay, [“Evidence for the 2π Decay of the K₂⁰ Meson”](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.13.138), *Physical Review Letters* 13 (1964): 138–140; Brookhaven’s [experiment history](https://www.bnl.gov/bnlweb/history/nobel/1980.php). The experiment used a spark-chamber spectrometer. A bubble-chamber photograph alone would not establish CP violation.
notes.evidence: Prior original-paper first-page apparatus excerpt and BNL history checked, christenson1964cp/bnl1980cp. The memoir does not identify her experiment.

notes.definition: C. S. Wu et al., [“Experimental Test of Parity Conservation in Beta Decay”](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.105.1413), *Physical Review* 105 (1957): 1413–1415, reporting the directional asymmetry of beta emission from polarized cobalt-60.
notes.evidence: Prior original publication and experiment description inspected, wu1957parity. “A decade earlier” corrected to “a few years earlier.”

notes.definition: Particle Data Group, [“CP Violation in the Quark Sector”](https://pdg.lbl.gov/2025/reviews/rpp2025-rev-cp-violation.pdf) (2025), opening sections. Kobayashi and Maskawa’s three-generation explanation dates to 1973. The single CKM phase accounts for Standard Model quark-sector CP violation, not every possible source of CP violation.
notes.evidence: Prior PDG review opening pp.1–2 inspected, pdg2025cp. Scope explicitly narrowed in body.

notes.definition: Planck Collaboration, [“Cosmological parameters”](https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.06209) (2020), baryon density; A. Riotto and M. Trodden, [“Recent Progress in Baryogenesis”](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/9901362) (1999), Sakharov conditions; PDG [“CP Violation”](https://pdg.lbl.gov/2025/reviews/rpp2025-rev-cp-violation.pdf), on the insufficient Standard Model quark contribution. The roughly $6\times10^{-10}$ figure is a baryon-to-photon ratio, not a direct count of annihilated pairs.
notes.evidence: Planck abstract/parameters freshly inspected; baryogenesis author review and PDG asymmetry scope previously checked. Conditional symmetric-start statement replaces absolute no-CP/no-matter assertion.

notes.definition: Particle Data Group, [“Higgs Boson”](https://pdg.lbl.gov/2025/reviews/rpp2025-rev-higgs-boson.pdf) (2025), §§11.1–11.2; CERN, [“What is the Higgs boson?”](https://home.cern/science/physics/higgs-boson/what/). Mass generated through Higgs coupling is inertia, not a frictional slowing. ATLAS and CMS announced the boson’s discovery in July 2012.
notes.evidence: PDG cited passages previously checked; CERN explanation/discovery and teaching FAQ explicitly distinguishing friction inspected 2026-10-23.

notes.definition: Sean M. Carroll, [*Lecture Notes on General Relativity*, §8](https://ned.ipac.caltech.edu/level5/March01/Carroll3/Carroll8.html), on dynamical cosmological geometry. The matter–curvature sentence adapts John Archibald Wheeler’s familiar summary. Matter and spacetime geometry are coupled in general relativity, not identical substances.
notes.evidence: Prior primary lecture-text inspection, carroll1997gr. Wheeler formulation retained as an attributed adaptation, not exact direct quotation.

notes.definition: F. W. Dyson, A. S. Eddington and C. Davidson, [“A Determination of the Deflection of Light by the Sun’s Gravitational Field”](https://doi.org/10.1098/rsta.1920.0009), *Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society A* 220 (1920): 291–333, reporting the 1919 expeditions to Príncipe and Sobral. This was not relativity’s first successful comparison with observation: Einstein had already explained Mercury’s anomalous perihelion advance.
notes.evidence: Original paper metadata/title checked against the cited historical record; no fresh full-text inspection claimed. Earlier Mercury result is standard 1915 chronology; main text now says famous early test.

notes.definition: B. P. Abbott et al., [“Observation of Gravitational Waves from a Binary Black Hole Merger”](https://arxiv.org/abs/1602.03837), *Physical Review Letters* 116 (2016): 061102; LIGO, [discovery announcement](https://www.ligo.caltech.edu/LA/news/ligo20160211), 11 February 2016. GW150914 was recorded on 14 September 2015, with peak strain of order $10^{-21}$.
notes.evidence: 2026-10-23: collaboration announcement inspected; paper identity/abstract checked. Removed overly exact proton-width comparison, preserving scale.

notes.definition: Roger Penrose, *The Emperor’s New Mind* (1989), ch. 7, on gravitational entropy; Sean M. Carroll and Jennifer Chen, [“Does Inflation Provide Natural Initial Conditions for the Universe?”](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/0505037), *General Relativity and Gravitation* 37 (2005): 1671–1674. Their proposed resolution is not established. Gravitational entropy is subtle: thermal uniformity of matter does not make the complete gravitating universe a maximum-entropy state.
notes.evidence: 2026-10-23: Carroll/Chen abstract inspected, full introductory low-entropy/black-hole argument read in author HTML. Penrose is retained as a bibliographic intellectual antecedent; not newly read in this run.

notes.definition: Alan H. Guth, [“Inflationary universe: A possible solution to the horizon and flatness problems”](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.23.347), *Physical Review D* 23 (1981): 347–356; PDG, [“Inflation”](https://pdg.lbl.gov/2025/reviews/rpp2025-rev-inflation.pdf), §§23.1–23.2. Starobinsky’s 1980 model and subsequent models by Linde and by Albrecht and Steinhardt are distinct foundational contributions. Guth’s original version had an unsuccessful exit mechanism; later models changed it.
notes.evidence: Prior original Guth abstract and PDG §23.1–2 checks. Text’s compact historical overview does not identify all inflationary models with false-vacuum trapping.

notes.definition: Particle Data Group, [“Inflation”](https://pdg.lbl.gov/2025/reviews/rpp2025-rev-inflation.pdf) (2025), observational constraints; Alan H. Guth, [“Eternal inflation and its implications”](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/0702178), *Journal of Physics A* 40 (2007): 6811–6826, on eternal inflation and its measure problem. Primordial tensor amplitudes depend on the model; a nondetection at one sensitivity does not rule out inflation as a class.
notes.evidence: Previously inspected PDG review/Guth author HTML. Observational baseline explicitly 2025 rather than a claim of live 2026 completeness. Stable incoming ID retained despite broader note content.

notes.definition: Wolfgang Pauli, [letter of 4 December 1930](https://cds.cern.ch/record/264021/), CERN Pauli Archive, opening “Liebe Radioaktive Damen und Herren.” The English salutation is the customary translation. The proposal addressed missing beta-decay energy and angular momentum.
notes.evidence: 2026-10-23: original archive record and CERN biographical excerpt inspected, including salutation/date. Brief English rendering, no unidentified long translation.

notes.definition: Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences, [scientific background to the 2015 Nobel Prize in Physics](https://www.nobelprize.org/uploads/2017/09/advanced-physicsprize2015.pdf), on the 1956 detection and Super-Kamiokande/SNO oscillation evidence; John N. Bahcall, [“How the Sun Shines”](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/themes/how-the-sun-shines/), on solar neutrinos. Oscillations require differences of squared neutrino masses and thus at least two nonzero masses, extending the original minimal Standard Model.
notes.evidence: 2026-10-23: Nobel technical-background and author essay excerpts inspected. Body uses an order-of-magnitude flux instead of claiming a detector-specific number.

notes.definition: John S. Bell, [“On the Einstein Podolsky Rosen Paradox”](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysicsPhysiqueFizika.1.195), *Physics* 1 (1964): 195–200; Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences, [scientific background to the 2022 Nobel Prize in Physics](https://www.nobelprize.org/uploads/2026/05/advanced-physicsprize-2022-5.pdf). Bell tests constrain local hidden-variable accounts under assumptions including independence of measurement settings. They neither supply faster-than-light messaging nor rule out every hidden-variable interpretation.
notes.evidence: 2026-10-23: Nobel technical-background excerpt inspected; original Bell metadata retained. Qualification distinguishes locality from hidden variables in general; Einstein phrase is short familiar translated attribution.

notes.definition: Michael R. Douglas, [“The statistics of string/M theory vacua”](https://arxiv.org/html/hep-th/0303194), *Journal of High Energy Physics* (2003), article 046, on counting candidate vacua and the vacuum-selection problem; Raphael Bousso, [“TASI Lectures on the Cosmological Constant”](https://arxiv.org/abs/0708.4231) (2007), §6.4, preprint p. 28, gives the illustrative flux-counting example. The often-quoted $10^{500}$ is an illustrative landscape scale, not an experimentally established count of universes or merely a count of geometric foldings.
notes.evidence: 2026-10-23: original abstract/introduction and numerical estimate passage inspected. Numerical example checked in the indexed primary text of Raphael Bousso’s TASI lectures, preprint p.28, §6.4; no observed multiverse claimed.

notes.definition: Carlo Rovelli and Lee Smolin, [“Discreteness of area and volume in quantum gravity”](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/9411005) (1995); Abhay Ashtekar, Tomasz Pawlowski and Parampreet Singh, [“Quantum Nature of the Big Bang”](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/0604013), *Physical Review Letters* 96 (2006): 141301. The bounce result cited is for a homogeneous, isotropic model with a massless scalar field; it is not an established history of our universe or a generic conclusion of all loop quantum gravity.
notes.evidence: Prior primary abstracts checked, rovellismolin1995geometry/ashtekar2006bounce. Model boundary incorporated in body.

notes.definition: Luca Bombelli et al., [“Space-time as a causal set”](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.59.521), *Physical Review Letters* 59 (1987): 521–524; Tomasz Konopka, Fotini Markopoulou and Lee Smolin, [“Quantum Graphity”](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/0611197) (2006); J. Ambjørn, J. Jurkiewicz and R. Loll, [“Emergence of a 4D World from Causal Quantum Gravity”](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/0404156) (2004). These are different proposals for microscopic structure and emergent geometry.

notes.definition: Mark Van Raamsdonk, [“Building up spacetime with quantum entanglement”](https://arxiv.org/abs/1005.3035), *General Relativity and Gravitation* 42 (2010): 2323–2329; Shinsei Ryu and Tadashi Takayanagi, [“Holographic Derivation of Entanglement Entropy from AdS/CFT”](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/0603001) (2006). notes.definition: Helge Kragh, [“An Anthropic Myth: Fred Hoyle’s Carbon-12 Resonance Level”](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00407-010-0068-8), *Archive for History of Exact Sciences* 64 (2010): 721–751; author preprint [“When is a prediction anthropic?”](https://philsci-archive.pitt.edu/5332/1/3alphaphil.pdf). Wilson, [“A Measurement of Excess Antenna Temperature at 4080 Mc/s”](https://articles.adsabs.harvard.edu/pdf/1965ApJ...142..419P), *Astrophysical Journal* 142 (1965): 419–421; R. H.
